result.decision_rationale:
The required unit gate passed. Ten prior fixes are verified. Two publication failure paths still leave the PR with an inaccurate account of what was superseded. Withdrawn requests also escape the remote history check, and retrying an older saved file can reinstate an instruction the owner later withdrew.

## Continuation for Claude

Base amendment corrections on which request, verdict, and receipt parts actually reached the PR. Close the visible record for the affected round, keep delivered request parts subject to the remote integrity check, and exclude withdrawn parts from pending work. Use the recorded source path and message digest to recognize a previously applied submission across revisions. Preserve the tested behavior for a newly received message with identical wording.

Use the existing controller and Git fixtures to exercise failed verdict and receipt publication, a changed historical request comment, and replay after an intervening amendment. Complete R1-F5’s same-enrollment test through publication of the safe replacement. Keep the repairs within amendment admission, publication, status, and their tests. Run the required unit gate through the pinned controller on the pushed correction.

executed_verification: The CLI transcript records the guarded push of b2fd0c4 to claude/continuation-handoff followed by verify --gate unit through the pinned package. The controller receipt names the full candidate SHA, exit 0, 615.8 seconds, and an unchanged worktree.
The gate log records 253 tests run, with 252 passing and one live-smoke test skipped. Its SHA-256 matches the receipt: a170ef50de522f3bf9fb357d96e4bf3a8f7b0b0a0834dae2b6241c810f3d06c6.

Read-only Git inspection confirmed parent 7add367b6274fd58af3b2bb49272a203f4624061, tree b346f8753983bf37ad03f2636855b5cca1e7f817, and the stated merge base. The mission and guidance hashes matched the request. The feature diff passed git diff --check.
inspected: The mission and owner addendum, guidance revision 1, all twelve prior findings and dispositions, the developer report, CLI transcript, gate receipt, and gate log.
The full feature diff and the correction from 7add367 to H, including the controller, three prompt templates, behavior fixtures, operator guide, and protocol.
limitations: Reviewer verification used read-only snapshot inspection. Test execution is attributed to the recorded controller gate. The earlier 18-test focused run preceded the replacement commit.

The behavior fixtures use real Git repositories, locks, controller state, and archive commits with simulated Claude, Codex, and GitHub boundaries. The supplemental live-model gates were not run. Notification in the launching conversation is a supervisor duty.
required_gaps: R1-F5 still needs the posted review request containing the safe amendment after an unpublishable submission was refused in that same enrollment.
The correction needs fixture evidence for supersession after failed verdict and receipt POSTs, remote integrity of a withdrawn request’s delivered parts, and replay of an older saved submission.
source_inspection_only: The remaining publication defects follow from tracing apply_amendment, retire_verdict, retire_receipts, missing_publications, and status. The recorded fixtures stop short of the failing observations described below.
The older-file replay follows from amendment_refusal comparing the submission with the current revision alone.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: At the validated boundary, apply_amendment calls retire_verdict alone. With zero visible verdict parts, it queues no correction to the posted request. At the finalize boundary, the mere presence of a pending final-status key suppresses the ready-verdict correction. The controller then publishes a reopened notice saying an earlier handoff was preserved above, even when its receipt was definitively rejected.
findings.blocking_rationale: The owner can see a request that will never receive a verdict, or a published ready verdict followed by a correction referring to a handoff that never appeared.
findings.expected: Identify the visible request or ready verdict by round and commit, and explain why it is no longer current. A handoff correction should refer to a handoff that actually reached the PR.
findings.requested_correction: Use confirmed publication state when choosing the correction. Close a posted request when its validated verdict was retired before publication. Retire a definitively unsent receipt and correct the published ready verdict it would have followed.
findings.requested_evidence: Apply an amendment after a definitive rejection of the verdict POST, then exercise the corresponding rejection of the first handoff-receipt POST in a separate fixture. Assert the actual PR correction in each case, its round and commit, and zero additional obsolete reviewer launches.
findings.title: Failed verdict and receipt POSTs leave the wrong public record current
findings.trigger: An amendment arrives after the request was posted and its validated verdict could not be published, or after the ready verdict was posted and its first handoff receipt could not be published.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: retire_request marks the entire request superseded. missing_publications skips every part of that record, including confirmed comments. The archive uses their local outbox bodies, so a later handoff can report handoff_current true after a delivered comment disappears or changes. Conversely, status lists the withdrawn request indefinitely under pending_publications.
findings.blocking_rationale: The new retirement path bypasses an existing integrity check for substantive PR history and reports settled work as awaiting delivery.
findings.expected: Continue verifying the identity and body of each delivered request part when checking the handoff. Treat the undelivered suffix as withdrawn and the reconciled request as settled.
findings.requested_correction: Use the recorded part IDs when checking amendment-withdrawn requests for remote integrity and pending delivery. Preserve the archive and withdrawal correction without resending the suffix.
findings.requested_evidence: Take a partly delivered request through withdrawal and a later verified handoff. Show the settled request is absent from pending_publications. Edit or remove its previously delivered part on simulated GitHub and show status --remote detects the change.
findings.title: Withdrawing a request drops its delivered comments from remote verification
findings.trigger: An amendment withdraws a fully or partly posted request. A previously confirmed request comment is subsequently edited or removed before the next handoff check.

findings.actual: The replay check compares source and message_sha256 only with the selected revision. After A and then B are applied, retrying A’s original file passes admission, appends A as revision 3, and can launch development under it.
findings.blocking_rationale: A retry can reinstate a requirement the owner withdrew in B and consume another invocation without a newly received instruction. The playbook tells the supervisor that replaying an applied file is refused.
findings.expected: Recognize a previously applied saved submission after intervening revisions. Continue accepting genuinely new timestamped files that contain the same words.
findings.requested_correction: Check the existing revision history for the saved path and message digest before appending the submission.
findings.requested_evidence: Apply A, apply a conflicting B, and retry A’s original file. Assert that B stays selected and the counters and agent calls are unchanged. Then submit A’s words in a newly saved file and verify that this distinct decision is accepted.
findings.title: Retrying an older saved amendment makes it the newest owner instruction
findings.trigger: The supervisor retries the same saved submission after a different amendment has been applied.

acceptance_ids: B. Both roles receive the same effective instructions
findings.actual: The fixture verifies the unsafe refusal and applies the safe file, then scripts the developer to return paused. No review request containing that safe revision is published in this fixture. Successful publication elsewhere in the suite uses another enrollment.
findings.blocking_rationale: The preflight fix is present, but the disposition claims a same-enrollment publication observation that the cited test never reaches.
findings.expected: Observe the safe replacement in a published review request in the enrollment where the unsafe submission was refused, as requested in round 1.
findings.requested_correction: Extend the existing refusal fixture through a checkpoint-ready report and review-request publication for the safe amendment.
findings.requested_evidence: Assert the safe text, revision, and digest in the posted request after the unchanged refusal, and report the candidate-bound fixture result.
findings.title: The safe replacement test stops before publication
findings.trigger: A PR-safe amendment follows a submission refused by the publication sanitizer.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: Admission now checks the last report’s pending restoration. The gate exercises both refusal without a lock file and a shared lock appearing during the last PR lookup. The latter preserves state and STOP, then succeeds after the lock clears.

The lost-response fixture first refuses while the stored comment is hidden, then reconciles it by actor, marker, and body when visible. It records one request, one withdrawal, and zero obsolete reviewer calls.

The multipart fixture verifies suppression of the unsent suffix and archival of the delivered part. The finalize fixture verifies a correction before any receipt is queued. The failed-POST paths in the restated finding still leave visible work without an accurate correction.
queue normalizes the public body before hashing. The CRLF fixture checks the private rationale, following developer prompt, published rendering, archive, and current handoff.
The strict sanitizer now runs before selection, and the unsafe-input test confirms unchanged state. The requested publication of the following safe revision in the same enrollment remains unobserved.

Two separately saved messages with identical bytes now produce two ordered labels and both reach the developer prompt. The immediate retry of the same file is refused. R2-F2 concerns retrying an older file after another decision.

The fixture applies an amendment to a preserved handoff in PAUSED/done after a PR-read failure and to a stopped review with an ended attempt whose PID was reused. An unfinished attempt still refuses admission.

Reloaded state preserves the returning invocation’s bindings on three reports across two amendments. last_report_instructions matches the paused report, and last_report_for prevents its use for review.

The playbook distinguishes round allocation, process start, and return. The status fixture shows a matching round with no attempt before dispatch, then an ended successful attempt whose reviewer input contains the amendment.

The activation fixture follows ACTIVE/review through the existing stop file to PAUSED and applies the amendment without dispatching the old review. A separate fixture confirms that raising max-rounds leaves an exhausted developer-invocation cap in force.

The reviewer prompt requires the amendment label and withdrawn requirement in the assessment rationale. The fixture checks that citation in the ledger, PR review, and archive while the unrelated finding stays blocking.

The fixture configures a required project gate, obtains a report-correction prompt containing the amendment and missing gate, then proceeds with a controller-recorded passing receipt for the amended candidate.

summary.delivered_behavior: The fixtures demonstrate reviewer continuation through publication, developer correction, archive, and handoff. Owner amendments reach both roles, require a fresh report, preserve earlier instructions and spent counters, and support reassessment of withdrawn requirements.
remaining_owner_review: After a corrected and verified handoff, Howie decides whether to accept draft PR #6 and authorize installation or activation for any existing enrollment.
summary.scope_reviewed: Final checkpoint for howardreith/development-process PR #6, including the complete mission, all twelve prior dispositions, and the affected publication, readiness, and operator-status paths.
